title: Naval on reading, habits, decisions, and happiness: The Knowledge Project interview
summary: Naval explains how he reads (skim, drop books freely, reread greats), why habits and internal states are trainable, and how he makes decisions via mental models, long-term thinking, and avoiding mistakes rather than predicting. He also covers trust and integrity, picking founders, and why happiness is the absence of desire.

principles.text: Read daily; the habit matters more than what you read, and reading what excites you compounds.
principles.quote: the best books to read are the ones that books or blogs or Twitter or whatever anything with ideas and information and learning the best wants to read it are the ones that you're excited about reading all the time

principles.text: Treat books like a blog archive: skim, jump around, and drop them without guilt.
principles.quote: I'll skim through a large number of books I'll put down I'll jump around back forward middle until I find a part that's interesting I'll just consume that piece and I won't feel guilty about having to finish the entire book

principles.text: Decision quality drives nonlinear returns because of leverage; load your head with mental models.
principles.quote: decision making is everything and in fact someone who makes decisions right 80% of time so 70% of time will be valued and compensate in the market hundreds of times more

principles.text: Success is avoiding mistakes and rigging asymmetric payoffs, not predicting winners.
principles.quote: I think being successful is just about not making mistakes it's not about you know having correct judgments it's about avoiding the incorrect judgments

principles.text: Think long term: compounding applies to relationships and work, so avoid short-term dealers.
principles.quote: I think all the benefits in life come from compound interests whether in money or in relationships or love or health or activities or habits

principles.text: Back founders who think long term, know the space, and love the work enough to commit for a decade.
principles.quote: go find the thing you can commit to for 10 years because that's how long it's going to take minimum to get a good outcome and you have to enjoy the journey
